summary: Plan on a strong or creative model, optionally have a model critique the plan, then execute or review on a cheaper instruction-following model (e.g. Opus plan / Sonnet execute).
steps: Plan with the frontier model | Critique the plan | Hand the plan to a cheaper executor | Use executor or reviewer to find gaps
tools: Claude Code plan mode, Opus, o3, Sonnet, Codex
jarvis_use: Frontier tier for the plan and critique, mid tier for multi-step execution.

name: Cheap bulk step, strong final step
summary: Cheap model classifies, ingests, gathers or drafts; a stronger model decides, writes the reply, does final polish or synthesizes over the gathered data.
steps: Attach a cheap model to classify, gather or draft nodes | Attach a stronger model to the final write or synthesis node | Name nodes by model
tools: OpenRouter, n8n, GPT-4.1 mini, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, GPT-5 mini, GPT-5, Opus, Fable, GLM 5.2
jarvis_use: Small tier for classify/ingest/draft steps, frontier for final output.

name: Deterministic first (vending machine vs slot machine)
summary: For each step ask whether it must be triggered by a human and whether it needs AI at all. Predictable, repetitive work goes to scripts or plain workflows; only messy, judgment-heavy input goes to an agent constrained by SOPs.
steps: Ask: must I trigger this? | Ask: does this step need AI? | Default to the cheapest deterministic option | Constrain agentic steps with SOPs and tools
jarvis_use: Jev labels each step deterministic (shell/saved procedure, no LLM) or reasoning before choosing a tier.

name: When to delegate / independence test before fan-out
summary: Delegate when work would dump output you won't reread, spans many files, repeats, splits into independent parallel pieces, or needs an unbiased fresh reviewer. Stay inline for quick edits, dependent steps, work needing full context or questions to the user; use teams when agents must talk.
steps: Ask the 'pile I'll never reread' question | Check use signals | Check skip signals | Ask whether pieces are independent | Choose inline, sub-agent or team; don't over-spawn
jarvis_use: Pre-spawn gate for Jarvis sub-agents.

name: Pick scheduler by constraint (routine vs desktop task vs /loop)
summary: Cloud routines run with the machine off but without local files; desktop scheduled tasks need the machine on, read local files and survive restarts; /loop dies with the session. Stated quotas and minimum intervals are source claims.
steps: Local files needed: desktop task | Machine off: cloud routine | Sub-hour cadence: desktop task or /loop | Must survive restart: not /loop | Check quotas
jarvis_use: Recurring local work goes to launchd-style jobs that survive reboot; Jarvis also needs its own resume-after-reboot.

name: Two-speed: quick fetch vs verified run
summary: A plain request returns raw data fast; a /goal run with enrichment, verification passes and debate takes much longer but is higher quality. Pick the speed by need.
steps: Raw data fast: simple request | High quality: goal loop plus verification | Budget time accordingly
jarvis_use: Jev labels a request quick or verified; verified runs need an independent verifier, which Jarvis lacks.

name: Right-size the model / cheapest model that passes
summary: If a task is a 5, don't pay for a 10. Route each task to the cheapest model that meets its quality bar; reserve premium models for hard, judgment or taste-heavy work, and prefer strong-but-cheaper frontier over the priciest model.
steps: Rate task difficulty | Define the quality bar | Test cheaper models against it | Route to the cheapest passing model
tools: Jev, Claude Haiku, Claude Sonnet, Claude Opus, Fable
jarvis_use: Jev tiering exists; missing is a per-task quality check to confirm the cheaper model passes.

name: Token thrift can cost quality
summary: Fewer tokens is not automatically better; the more token-efficient run produced a much weaker artifact. Check whether the cost ratio buys a matching quality gap.
steps: Compare quality next to spend | Ask whether quality gap matches cost ratio | Pick on quality per dollar per task class
jarvis_use: Cost meter exists; Jev should weigh a quality signal, not just cost, for creative/showpiece work.

name: Task-type to model mapping (cross-lab specialists)
summary: Route sub-tasks by perceived model strength: e.g. writing/planning, coding/review, research/facts, images, personal or edgy questions; specialize coding tools by role. The mappings are anecdotal hypotheses.
steps: Name the job type | Assign the model or tool best on that type from your own evals | Label gut feel separately from metrics
tools: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, ChatGPT, Grok, ACQ AI
jarvis_use: Jev pools span providers; a tested task-kind to model map is not yet in place.

name: Model routing table (cost / intelligence / taste)
summary: Give the agent a table of every available model, including delegates like Codex or open-source models, scored on cost, intelligence and taste, plus workflow-specific columns.
steps: List all models | Score cost, intelligence, taste | Add workflow columns | Put table in agent context
jarvis_use: Make the table Jev's routing config and consult it when picking a sub-agent model.

name: Effort ladder
summary: Default to medium or high; high for big builds, extra-high or max only for capability-sensitive work or a stuck bug; low for routine. Tune effort before blaming or switching the model, and reset defaults that drift upward.
steps: Classify routine / normal / capability-sensitive | Pick effort accordingly | On laziness or over-engineering, re-run at a different effort | Check defaults each session
jarvis_use: Jev picks tier and escalates; per-call effort level and retry-at-higher-effort before model switch are not explicit.

name: Stronger model at lower effort
summary: Compare effort levels across model generations; a newer model at low effort may match an older one at extra-high for less cost.
steps: Compare effort charts | Find the lowest matching effort on the new model | Confirm quality on own tasks
jarvis_use: Jev may prefer new-model low effort when evals show parity.

name: Effort budgeting by task size
summary: Scale tool calls to the request: about 1 for a simple fact, 3-5 for a medium task, 5-10 for deep research or comparisons.
steps: Classify simple / medium / deep | Set call budget | Escalate explicitly to exceed it
jarvis_use: Jev returns a call budget alongside the tier; repetition brake exists but no size-based budget.

name: Model switch breaks cache
summary: Each model has its own cache; switching mid-thread (including opusplan's plan/execute toggle) rereads all history uncached. Route at task or sub-agent start and hand off compactly.
steps: Avoid mid-thread switches | Know opusplan toggles models | Weigh recache cost against executor savings
jarvis_use: Jarvis has prompt cache and escalation; escalation should pass a compact handoff, not full history.

name: Explore on frontier, distill to a skill, repeat on cheaper model
summary: First run on the strongest model; capture the working pipeline as a skill; re-run later on a cheaper model; use cheaper models for verification sub-agents.
steps: First run on frontier | Save pipeline as skill | Re-run on mid tier with the skill | Verify with cheaper sub-agents
jarvis_use: Procedural memory exists; skills library loading and auto-downgrade for jobs with a saved procedure are missing.

name: Desk vs pocket agent split
summary: Deep build and coding go to a desk CLI agent; quick check-ins, comms, reminders and crons go to an always-on mobile/messaging agent; no long coding through the phone channel.
steps: Classify deep vs quick | Deep: desk coding agent | Quick/remote: handle in Jarvis loop
tools: Claude Code, Codex, Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, Telegram, Grok Bot (Cursor)
jarvis_use: Jarvis tags requests deep-build (hand to Claude Code/Codex via shell) vs light ops (do directly) and refuses long coding over voice.

name: Agent-feature ladder (ask, skill, sub-agent, team, /goal, workflow)
summary: Quick thing: ask. Repeated: skill. Messy side task: sub-agent. Crew that must talk: team. Iterate until criteria met: /goal. Giant parallel job: workflow. Climb only as needed.
steps: Classify the task | Pick the lowest rung that solves it | Skills and tools plug into any rung
jarvis_use: Jarvis has ask and procedural memory; skills, sub-agents, teams and fan-out are missing.

name: Width vs depth: done-loop vs fan-out
summary: A /goal loop iterates one objective until a check passes; a workflow fans many agents across a fixed plan. Combining both is powerful but expensive.
steps: Single objective needing iteration: done-loop | Many independent pieces: fan-out | Approval before combining
jarvis_use: Loop-until-verified for single goals, parallel fan-out for batches, never both without Evens's approval.

name: Mode gate: NO_ACTION when clients are parked
summary: Every hunt or outreach step first checks whether clients are parked; if so the result is NO_ACTION and the step waits for Evens to tag an icp_id.
steps: Check mode | If parked: NO_ACTION | Ask Evens or leave queued
jarvis_use: Jarvis holds sends for OK; an explicit BUILDING-mode check before lead/outreach steps is not built in.

name: Hosted voice widget vs self-hosted socket
summary: Hosted platforms run the persistent websocket and give an embed; self-hosted Gemini Live is easy on localhost but needs a persistent process, key storage and connection handling for production.
steps: Prototype on localhost | Decide hosted vs own process | Plan keys, connections, hosting
jarvis_use: BUS300 decision input; production hosting is an architecture promotion for Evens.

name: Layer pyramid / three-question build tree
summary: Four layers: custom GPT/project, no-AI workflow, AI workflow, agent. Ask: human in loop every time? 100% logic? fixed order? Pick the lowest layer that works and re-classify after real runs.
steps: Ask three yes/no questions | Pick lowest layer | Ship smallest | Observe runs and re-classify
jarvis_use: Pre-build classifier for any new Jarvis routine.

name: Variable-pass retrieval exception
summary: Even with a fixed order, use an agent when the number of knowledge-base searches varies per case, so it can do 0..N passes.
steps: Map the manual process | Check whether retrieval count varies | If yes, agent decides with a cap
jarvis_use: The operator loop already decides how many searches to run; the repetition brake caps it.

name: Stay interactive if you edit every run
summary: If output needs revision every time, keep it interactive; automate only once output is stable.
steps: Count edits per run | If frequent, stay manual | Promote when stable
jarvis_use: Jarvis works interactively per line; taste-heavy tasks stay with Evens in the loop.

name: Overkill check before building a trigger
summary: Before automating, compare to doing it manually; build a trigger only for real cadence.
steps: Describe the automation | Compare to manual once | Build only for repeated runs
jarvis_use: Jarvis defaults to doing the task directly and asks before creating any scheduler.

name: Native tool before custom workflow round-trip
summary: For common actions use a built-in platform tool; reserve custom n8n round-trips for custom work.
steps: Check for a native tool | Use it if it covers the action | Else build a workflow tool
jarvis_use: Prefer built-in tools/MCP over custom workflows; no explicit preference order today.

name: Partial agent coverage
summary: Ask what share of a process an agent can do, always route that share to the agent, keep trust-heavy steps with humans.
steps: Break into steps | Estimate agent share | Route that share to the agent | Hand human-only steps to Evens
jarvis_use: Jarvis does its part and holds sends/pay/delete and login walls for Evens via ask_owner.

name: Pin model and effort for scheduled jobs
summary: An automation defaulted to an older model and ran slowly; set model and reasoning explicitly and avoid usage-heavy fast modes.
steps: Open automation settings | Set model and reasoning | Retrigger | Leave speed standard
jarvis_use: Jev picks per job; scheduled jobs should store their pinned tier.

name: Re-tune tier thresholds when limits change
summary: When provider session limits grow, relax aggressive downgrading where quality matters, but keep context hygiene.
steps: Check limit changes | Reduce downgrading where quality matters | Keep context discipline
jarvis_use: Jev thresholds reviewed when provider limits change.

name: Per-workspace engine selection
summary: Sibling folders, one with a provider-routing settings.local.json and one without; the launch directory chooses the engine so experiments don't leak into the main setup.
steps: Create two sibling dirs | Put routing settings in one | Launch from the folder for the wanted engine | Confirm model in banner
jarvis_use: Pin Jev routes per workspace config instead of global settings.

name: Choose retrieval by what a human would do
summary: Filter for known fields and small subsets, SQL for totals/rankings/trends, full context for summaries and ordered content, vector search for a local answer in a large corpus.
steps: Ask what a careful human would do | Map to filter / SQL / full / vector
jarvis_use: Jev classify step that picks the retrieval method per question.

name: Persona debate panel for decisions
summary: 3-7 personas research independently and debate, optionally to consensus; the human reads the debate. Consensus mode can run away on tokens; usage figures are claims.
steps: Define personas | Independent research | Debate with cap | Hand transcript to Evens
jarvis_use: Capped cheap-tier debate for hard choices; Evens gets the transcript, not a decision.

name: One lane / one ship per session
summary: Classify the session path before acting, work one system per session, and have the principal pick at most one ship.
steps: Classify session path | One system per session | Ask Evens to pick at most one ship
jarvis_use: Jarvis classifies each request into one lane and asks before adding a second deliverable.

name: Pain-first tool adoption (weight-off-shoulders filter)
summary: Learn what a new tool does, but adopt it only if it removes a real current pain; viral is not a reason.
steps: Know where the load is | Ask if the release removes it | Adopt only if yes
jarvis_use: Score new tools/signals against BUS300 before proposing; depends on signal ingestion, which is missing.

name: Productivity-dip rule for stack switches
summary: Every switch costs a temporary dip; switch only if the end-state line ends above the current trajectory. The 20% figure is the speaker's estimate.
steps: Assume a dip | Estimate post-dip line | Switch only if it ends higher
jarvis_use: Jarvis states the expected dip and end state when proposing a migration; Evens decides.

name: Kill on opportunity cost
summary: An opportunity is good or bad only relative to the cost of pursuing it versus the main line of work.
steps: List the signal | Compare to main line | Decide continue or kill | Record the decision
jarvis_use: Jarvis frames side ideas against BUS300; keep/kill is Evens's call.

name: Use NL builders for linear workflows only
summary: A natural-language workflow builder handled linear paths but produced broken orchestrator/sub-agent systems.
steps: Classify linear vs multi-agent | Generator for linear | Hand-build or audit multi-agent
jarvis_use: Only relevant if Jarvis generates n8n workflows; label linear vs agentic first.

name: Tier selection by cost and capability
summary: Small tier for cheap bulk work, mid tier as default, frontier for hard reasoning (keep under about 20%); output tokens cost more than input.
steps: Default execution to mid tier | Send bulk reading and formatting to small tier | Reserve frontier for planning and hard reasoning | Watch output-heavy tasks
jarvis_use: Jev already routes small/mid/frontier; cap frontier share and watch output-heavy jobs.

name: Per-step model routing (planner, reasoner, stylist)
summary: Split a job into steps and route each to the cheapest model that fits: a small model plans or summarizes into structured fields, a reasoning model writes content, a strong writer model turns it into HTML.
steps: Identify plan, think and format steps | Route plan/format to cheap tier with structured output fields | Route think step to reasoning model | Pass step output as next step's input
tools: n8n, OpenRouter, GPT-5 mini, OpenAI o3, Claude Sonnet 4.5
jarvis_use: Jev picks a tier per job today; extend it to route individual steps within a job to different models.

name: Choose model per sub-agent
summary: Set gather or search sub-agents to cheaper models and keep frontier for synthesis.
steps: Decide sub-agent model by task difficulty | Use cheap tiers for gather agents
jarvis_use: Blocked on sub-agents, which Jarvis lacks; once sub-agents exist, Jev assigns tiers per sub-agent.

name: Cheap or local models wrapped as skills
summary: Wrap a call to a cheaper or local model in a skill the main session can invoke.
steps: Pick the sub-task | Create a skill that calls the cheaper/local model | Invoke from main session
jarvis_use: Needs a skills library loader; then expose Jev cheap tiers as callable skills.

name: Cap effort at high; change model instead of effort
summary: Keep reasoning effort at high by default; higher modes overthink and over-delegate at more cost. Switch models for cost/quality trade-offs and check cost-vs-score curves before raising effort.
steps: Default effort to high | Escalate only with a reason | Prefer switching models | Compare outcome vs cost when testing higher effort
jarvis_use: Make 'effort = high, escalate model not effort' an explicit Jev default and log when effort is raised.

name: Same-prompt, same-harness model bakeoff with cost/time/token ledger
summary: Run the identical prompt on the same codebase and harness with each model (including cheap vs frontier one-shot design prompts); record cost, wall time and tokens, compare outputs, and ask whether the pricier model is worth its price multiple.
steps: Fix harness and prompt | Run each model on identical inputs | Record cost, time, input/output tokens | Compare outputs plus ledger; judge price multiple
jarvis_use: Per-job cost meter exists; missing is a same-task cross-model ledger that grounds Jev routing in Jarvis's own runs.

name: Compare outputs by the wrapper, not just the model
summary: Same model gives very different results depending on harness, skills, hooks, MCP, memory and docs; record the environment with every comparison and fix the harness before swapping models.
steps: Hold the wrapper fixed or note differences | List skills/hooks/MCP/memory present | Invest in wrapper before switching models
jarvis_use: Ledger rows record harness version and context used alongside model results.

name: Golden-task replay on a new model; default first, swap after eval
summary: On a new release, run your regular workflows unchanged on it before routing real work; start with a default model and swap only after an evaluation shows it is better for that use case.
steps: Pick regular workflows as golden tasks | Run unchanged on the new model | Note interpretation, stopping and verification differences | Swap routing only if better
jarvis_use: A fixed set of Jarvis golden tasks replayed before Jev adds a model to any pool.

name: Open-ended creative probe
summary: Give a new model an open creative goal (build anything as an HTML document) to see its taste, range and time.
steps: Issue an open creative goal | Run same prompt on another model | Compare topic, interactivity, polish, time
jarvis_use: Low-stakes probe before routing creative jobs to a new model.

name: Harness-free diagram test with render-and-check
summary: Ask models in plain chat for Excalidraw JSON, render and compare; without verification, errors like clipped text show up.
steps: Ask for Excalidraw JSON | Render it | Compare accuracy and layout | Note errors a check would catch
jarvis_use: Jarvis can screenshot; missing is a mandatory render-and-check step before delivering diagrams (independent verifier).

name: Primary plus cross-provider fallback model
summary: Configure a main model and a fallback; a fallback on the same vendor via a different gateway fails together, so pick a different provider. Short-term memory keyed by channel/chat id lets the agent reuse recent object ids.
steps: Set main model | Configure fallback on a different provider | Key memory by conversation id
tools: n8n, OpenRouter, OpenAI, GPT 5.1, Claude Sonnet 3.5
jarvis_use: Jev has escalation across vendors but no defined per-route outage fallback; idle session continuation covers chat memory.

name: Fall back to previous model version when new one degrades
summary: Keep the earlier model version available and use it where it performs better on your tasks.
steps: Compare new vs previous on own tasks | Route to previous where better
jarvis_use: Jev keeps the prior version as a route option per task type, decided by ledger results.

name: Model-agnostic harness and open-weights hedge
summary: Model is the engine, harness the car, human the driver. Hosted closed models can be withdrawn, so keep procedures, memory and data model-agnostic, know an open-weights alternative (hosted if too big for local), and invest in owned processes and hardware.
steps: List closed models the workflow depends on | Find an open-weights alternative | Use a hosted runner if too big for local | Keep harness and memory model-agnostic
jarvis_use: Jarvis's procedural memory is model-independent and Jev spans several vendors; missing is a tested open-weights fallback route.

name: Closed vs local model compute tradeoff
summary: Hosted models perform well partly due to provider compute; local or VPS models need enough RAM/VRAM to run fast.
steps: Check RAM/VRAM vs model needs | Use hosted when local compute is too small
jarvis_use: Jev checks Mac RAM/VRAM and the resource floor before any local-model route.

name: One gateway credential for many models
summary: Create one router key (OpenRouter) stored once as a credential and reuse it across nodes and agent chat models; pick the model per step; unified billing and usage. Native nodes only when they offer a needed modality (e.g. Gemini document analysis).
steps: Create router account and key | Store as one credential | Reuse across nodes and agents | Pick model per step
jarvis_use: Jev already spans vendor pools via env-var-referenced credentials; key creation stays with Evens.

name: Route around a native-integration bug via the router
summary: When a new model errors on a native node (bad parameter values) but the older model works, isolate it, then call the same model through the router.
steps: Reproduce with a trivial prompt | Test older model on same integration | Retry same model via router
jarvis_use: Jarvis isolates by testing the prior model and reports; alternate routes go through Jev, never ad-hoc key swaps (rule 6).

name: Read real provider limits at call time
summary: Context window and price can differ between a router listing and the vendor console; check actual limits.
steps: Open router model comparison | Compare price and context window vs vendor
jarvis_use: Jev stores per-route context/price as read from the provider, tagged with a check date.

name: Native-only provider features
summary: Some features (OpenAI Responses built-in tools) are not available through aggregators; use the native credential when needed.
steps: If built-in tools needed, use native credential | Otherwise keep router
jarvis_use: Jev's routing table notes which features exist only on native APIs.

name: Provider built-in web/file search with context size, location and domain limits
summary: Enable the Responses API so the model itself does web or file search with citations; options for search context size, location targeting and an allowed-domains list.
steps: Enable Responses API | Add web and/or file search | Set context size, location, allowed domains
jarvis_use: Jarvis has its own web_search/fetch; add allowed-domain restriction for domain-specific lookups.

name: Try a newer same-family model before declaring a feature broken
summary: The allowed-domains filter failed on GPT-4.1 but worked on GPT-5 mini.
steps: Reproduce the failure | Switch to newer same-family model | Confirm behavior
tools: OpenAI Responses API, GPT-5 mini, GPT-4.1
jarvis_use: On a provider feature error, Jarvis retries on a newer model in the same family before reporting it broken.

name: Responses API extra options (cache key, metadata, service tier)
summary: Saved prompt id, service tier, safety id, conversation id, prompt cache key, metadata tags, logprobs.
steps: Enable Responses API | Set prompt cache key and metadata | Keep conversation memory local
jarvis_use: Jarvis has prompt cache; add metadata tags per job for traceability; keep memory local, not vendor conversation ids.

name: Subscription inference via Codex OAuth device code
summary: Pick OpenAI Codex as provider, sign in through the device-code flow, and use a ChatGPT subscription instead of metered API keys.
steps: Select Codex provider | Open auth URL and sign in | Paste device code | Pick model
jarvis_use: Jev could include subscription-backed routes where allowed; login is done by Evens.

name: Aggregator gateway for media generation
summary: Access many image/video models (Veo, Sora, Nano Banana, GPT Image) through one aggregator (Kie.ai, FAL.ai); prototype in the provider playground, copy the HTTP request, use fast variants to cut cost, split create vs edit models.
steps: Prototype prompt in playground | Copy HTTP/curl request | Call via one stored credential | Pick fast variant when good enough | Gate on quote and OK
tools: Kie.ai, FAL.ai, OpenRouter, Veo 3.1, Sora 2, Nano Banana, GPT Image 2
jarvis_use: If built, one gated media gateway; every paid generation needs a quote and Evens's per-job OK (media-gen-cost-gate); ArtCraft stays default.

name: Classify video-model jobs: offline diffusion vs real-time autoregressive
summary: Decide whether a job needs an offline coherent clip (diffusion; capped length, extend from last frame) or real-time steerable output (autoregressive next-frame world model).
steps: Ask if mid-shot input or unlimited length is needed | If no, diffusion clip; extend from last frame | If yes, autoregressive class
jarvis_use: Jarvis routes video requests to offline plates and never promises an interactive world model.

name: Camera-pose and promptable-event control of a world model
summary: Speculative: stream phone camera pose and text events into a world model and record output.
steps: Track pose via ARKit/ARCore | Stream as action input | Inject events | Record
jarvis_use: Research watch item only.

name: Voice LLM chosen on latency and cost
summary: Premium voices and smarter LLMs add latency; each model shows its own cost and ms; compare on live test calls (localhost felt slower than deployed), listen for slowness and repeated filler, and pick a model tested for instruction following.
steps: Note candidate latency and cost | Run same test call per model on the real surface | Listen for slowness and repeated filler | Check instruction following | Keep faster, smoother model
tools: ElevenLabs, Vapi, OpenAI GPT-4o, OpenAI GPT-4.1, Anthropic
jarvis_use: Jev routes voice turns to a fast-enough tier; missing is real-surface latency measurement and recorded A/B before swaps (BUS300-adjacent; live :4018 changes need Evens).

name: Iterate system prompts as a diff, then test
summary: Generate a prompt edit, review struck and added text, accept/refine/discard, then test by talking to the agent; repeat.
steps: Request the edit | Review diff | Accept, refine or discard | Test and repeat
jarvis_use: Jarvis prompt edits are shown as diffs and adopted only after a test run.

name: Context dumb-zone handoff before quality decays
summary: Large windows are a false ceiling; models degrade well before the limit and lost-in-the-middle worsens. Track context and hand off to a fresh session before the threshold instead of compacting.
steps: Track context use | Near threshold, write handoff and start fresh | Do not rely on mid-conversation details | Avoid compaction
jarvis_use: Jarvis keeps lean context (last 3 screenshots); add a per-model token budget that writes a handoff and continues fresh, which also serves resume-after-reboot.

name: Give the why (intent, audience, purpose)
summary: State the bigger task, who it is for, what they need and why each constraint exists (e.g. it is my writing style); this improves instruction following and steers retrieval to the right context files. Scope strong models ambitiously.
steps: State bigger task and audience | Attach reason to each constraint | Then make the request
jarvis_use: Jarvis task cards and sub-model calls carry a one-line goal, audience and why.

name: Tell it what to do, not what not to do
summary: Rewrite negative instructions as positive targets; keep a don't only with context.
steps: Rewrite don'ts as targets | Keep a don't only with its reason
jarvis_use: Jarvis phrases model instructions as positive specs; variant that differs from the don't-list method below.

name: Negative prompting with a do-not-act gate
summary: Brief like an intern: for questions the deliverable is an assessment; report and stop; don't fix, send, edit or delete until told to go; do the simplest thing that works.
steps: Add explicit don't-list | Define question deliverable as assessment | Report and stop until go
jarvis_use: Jarvis already holds send/pay/delete for Evens's OK with ask-then-resume.

name: Say less, not more
summary: With a capable model and good environment, a short steer plus the why beats numbered rule lists; standing behavior lives in system, memory and skill files.
steps: Replace rule lists with a short steer | Keep intent context | Move standing behavior into memory/skills
jarvis_use: Trim per-turn instructions; depends on a skills library to hold detail.

name: No standing 'explain your reasoning' line
summary: On one model a standing reveal-reasoning instruction can trigger refusals; ask for conclusions plus evidence instead.
steps: Remove reveal-reasoning lines | Ask for conclusion plus evidence
jarvis_use: Audit Jarvis system prompts for reveal-chain-of-thought lines.

name: Observable-behavior specs instead of vague adjectives
summary: Turn vague instructions ('off brand', 'more charismatic') into observable black-and-white behaviors and use them as prompts and checks.
steps: Find adjective instructions | Rewrite as observable criteria | Use as prompts and checks
jarvis_use: Jarvis asks Evens to turn vague feedback into concrete checks and stores them as testable criteria for a verifier.

name: Ask to explain or test, not for an opinion
summary: Opinion questions invite sycophancy; ask the model to explain how something works or test the claim against data.
steps: Phrase as explain-how | Turn opinion questions into tests
jarvis_use: Jarvis converts 'does this look right?' into a concrete check; needs an independent verifier to be reliable.

name: Treat vendor benchmarks and launch posts as claims
summary: Pick benchmarks matched to the job (long-horizon agentic, screen understanding, multi-step function calling) and re-test on your own tasks; read launch posts for access, dated plan windows and price multiples, which hint at capability differences.
steps: Pick job-matched benchmarks | Read availability, pricing and footnotes | Tag numbers UNVERIFIED | Confirm on own eval
tools: Vending-Bench 2, ScreenSpot Pro, Gemini 3.1 Flash Live, Claude
jarvis_use: Jarvis writes a short access/price/window note per new model with numbers tagged UNVERIFIED until its own eval or the vendor page confirms.

name: Price tier as a capability tell
summary: A model priced like a given tier should be benchmarked against same-priced peers; version numbering is another tell.
steps: Compare per-token price with peers | Benchmark against same-priced peer
jarvis_use: Benchmark a new model against the same-price model already in Jev's table.

name: Classify a 'frontier killer' as base model vs orchestrator
summary: Determine whether a release is a new LLM or a conductor routing to existing models; treat orchestrator benchmark wins as mixture results.
steps: Read architecture claim | Ask: new base model or multi-agent? | Treat orchestrator wins as mixture results
jarvis_use: Tag model announcements as base vs router before any routing-table change.

name: Fusion (broadcast + judge) vs split-and-delegate
summary: Send one prompt to several models with a judge merging, or split the task and delegate parts to specialists; both add perspective at a cost in speed and money.
steps: Fusion: broadcast to N models, judge merges | Delegate: split, specialists, combine | Weigh perspective vs latency and cost
jarvis_use: Jev could pick broadcast+judge for high-stakes single answers and split-delegate (needs sub-agents) for multi-part tasks, with cost noted.

name: Managed file search instead of a custom RAG pipeline (claim)
summary: Drop docs into a managed file-search store for embeddings and chat instead of building chunk/embed/vector pipelines; the cost claim is unexplained.
steps: Use managed store | Verify cost and answer quality
jarvis_use: Candidate for low-stakes doc Q&A only after cost and quality are verified.

name: Diagnose method vs compute vs data
summary: Neural nets stalled for lack of hardware and labeled data, not method; identify which blocks progress before rewriting.
steps: Identify blocker type | Get matched hardware or data | Use a shared benchmark
jarvis_use: When a Jarvis capability fails, classify the blocker as method, compute or data first.

name: Give the goal, not micro-steps (AlexNet lesson)
summary: Let the system learn the approach from full data and objective rather than prescribing intermediate features; measure on a shared benchmark.
steps: Give full context and objective | Do not prescribe steps | Measure result
jarvis_use: Give Jarvis goal plus context and verify the result instead of micro-instructions.

name: Backpropagation as a post-mortem analogy
summary: Trace error backward and assign blame to each step in proportion to its contribution before changing anything.
steps: Compute output error | Trace back step by step | Adjust the responsible steps
jarvis_use: Procedural memory post-mortems attribute a failed run to the steps that caused it.

name: Perceptron and transformer history (background)
summary: Perceptron learned weights from examples (1958); transformers read sequences in parallel and next-token pretraining led to GPT and ChatGPT.
steps: Labeled examples adjust weights | Parallel attention plus next-token pretraining at scale
jarvis_use: Background knowledge only.

name: Connection inventory, then connect one source at a time
summary: Audit where you look each week (revenue, customers, calendar, comms, tasks/PM, meetings, knowledge) plus apps, bookmarks and open tabs; map each to its tool; connect tier-1 sources one at a time via API, MCP or CLI.
steps: List weekly lookups by category: revenue, customers, calendar, internal/external comms, tasks/PM, meetings, knowledge | Add desktop apps, paid software, bookmarks, open tabs/history (Safari tabs with Evens's permission) | Map each category to the tool(s) where it lives | For each, find CLI/API/MCP | Connect and prove one at a time, tier-1 first
tools: Stripe, QuickBooks, Google Workspace, ClickUp, Slack, Fireflies, Skool, Google Drive
jarvis_use: Jarvis builds a connector backlog from Evens's real lookups (it can read Safari tabs) and wires/proves one connector at a time.

name: Credentials in a vault or named credential, never in the prompt
summary: Service auth lives in OAuth connectors, a named vault, or a reusable named credential (n8n Bearer/Gemini credential, Integrations page); raw keys only as env vars for approved services; never pasted into prompts or files.
steps: Prefer OAuth connector when available | Else store the key once as a named credential or env var | Reference by name in calls | Owner creates/pastes keys and completes OAuth | Broken connector: report for re-auth, do not route around
tools: Claude Managed Agents vault, Claude connectors, n8n credentials, Vapi Integrations, Google AI Studio
jarvis_use: Jarvis references env var names / connector auth only; OAuth consent and key creation are Evens's action; rule 6 on broken connectors.

name: Scoped read-only API key per agent
summary: Create a dedicated key per agent/connector scoped to only the resource needed; deny edit/delete/team actions.
steps: Create a dedicated key for the agent | Scope to read only the needed resource | Deny edit/delete/team | Reference via env var
jarvis_use: Each Jarvis connector uses its own least-privilege key referenced by env var name.

name: Keys in .env so integrations survive a harness switch
summary: Desktop one-click connectors are tied to that app; keys in a project .env plus scripts/recipes in a plain folder carry over to any harness.
steps: Keep API key names in a project .env | Keep integrations as scripts/recipes in the folder | Use desktop connectors knowing they won't carry over
jarvis_use: Keep Jarvis integrations as workspace scripts + env var names usable by any Mac harness.

name: Install an MCP from the vendor command or by asking the agent
summary: Copy the vendor's Claude Code 'mcp add' command, or ask the agent / plugin marketplace to add the integration; authorize in browser; confirm configured.
steps: Find the vendor's MCP install command or plugin | Ask the agent to install it (or click add) | Owner authorizes in browser | Confirm it shows as configured | Apply the repo install gate (license, archived, pin)
tools: Firecrawl MCP, Claude Code, Grok Bot plugins
jarvis_use: Jarvis may propose and install connectors under the repo install gate; OAuth grants stay with Evens.

name: Add a remote MCP as a custom connector, owner OAuth, verify toggled on
summary: Add custom connector with the vendor's remote MCP URL, owner completes OAuth (copy the full URL if terminal wrapping breaks the link), set scoped per-tool permissions, and confirm it is installed and on before any dependent task.
steps: Copy the remote MCP URL from the vendor's MCP page | Add custom connector, name it, paste URL | Surface the full OAuth link to Evens and wait | Restrict tool permissions (no blanket allow) | Verify connector is on before prompting dependent work
tools: Claude desktop/web connectors, Higgsfield MCP, Clay MCP
jarvis_use: Jarvis surfaces OAuth links and waits; starts with scoped permissions; never runs a tool-dependent task until the connector is confirmed on.

name: Integration route check: existing connector/plugin/CLI before raw glue
summary: Search existing connectors, plugins/MCPs and CLIs first; only if none exists fall back to API/OAuth path.
steps: Check for a connector | Check for a plugin/MCP | Check for a CLI | Pick one; else API/OAuth path
tools: Codex plugins, GitHub CLI, GitHub MCP, Supabase
jarvis_use: Jarvis checks for an MCP or CLI before driving a GUI (API/MCP over browser).

name: CLI-first tier: CLI, then API, then MCP
summary: MCP loads every tool schema each session; prefer an official/community CLI, else wrap the API as a CLI, MCP last; drop overlapping idle MCP servers.
steps: Search for a CLI | If none, wrap the API into a CLI | Use MCP only when nothing else works | Measure MCP context overhead | Remove overlapping MCP servers
tools: gws CLI, GitHub CLI, Playwright CLI, Higgsfield CLI
jarvis_use: Jarvis prefers shell CLIs (gh, gws) over loading big MCP toolsets.

name: Skill + CLI for each platform
summary: Give the agent a CLI plus a skill describing how and when to use it in your workflow; easier to maintain and lighter than MCP.
steps: Install and authorize the CLI | Write a skill card: when to use, commands, inputs | Agent calls the CLI through shell
tools: GitHub CLI, Google Workspace CLI, Archon
jarvis_use: Needs Jarvis skills-library loading; seed with gh and gws.

name: Wrap your own APIs into CLIs
summary: Turn APIs you already call into small local CLIs, then build a skill around each.
steps: Point the agent at an authenticated API | Ask it to turn it into a CLI with keys from env | Build a skill around it | Invoke in natural language
jarvis_use: Jarvis converts recurring API calls from procedural memory into local CLIs.

name: Defer MCP tool loading
summary: Load MCP tool schemas on demand (tool search) instead of all at session start; vendor claims large overhead cut.
steps: Measure MCP overhead | Defer schema loading until a tool is searched | Keep CLI > API > skills > MCP order
jarvis_use: Jarvis's mcp tool should fetch schemas lazily to keep context lean.

name: One broad MCP per domain (supermarket)
summary: Connect one server bundling many actions (scrape, crawl, search, extract, screenshot) and let the model pick tools and parameters.
steps: Connect one MCP covering the domain | Let the agent choose actions and parameters
jarvis_use: Prefer one broad MCP per domain over hand-wired endpoints, subject to the CLI-first tier.

name: Connect any tool from its API docs
summary: Find official API docs (or have the agent research them), list exact endpoints, owner supplies a scoped key via env, agent writes calls with retries, rate limits, pagination, tests and saves the recipe.
steps: Search '<tool> API documentation' | List exact endpoints needed | Ask Evens for a scoped key by env var name | Write calls with retries/pagination/rate limits | Test and save as a recipe/skill
jarvis_use: Standard Jarvis new-integration procedure using web_fetch + shell; recipe goes to procedural memory.

name: Least-privilege allowlist; never instance-wide execute or always-allow
summary: Expose only hand-enabled assigned tools; instance-level search-and-execute-anything plus always-allow is a wide blast radius; enumerate send/pay/delete verbs and allow one call at a time.
steps: Inventory MCP verbs | Flag send/pay/delete | Use curated assigned tools only | Enable each tool by hand | Never always-allow a send verb
jarvis_use: Jarvis gets an allowlist per job; side-effect MCP verbs go through ask_owner like Safari's held buttons.

name: Anti-pattern: drop auth to make a connector work
summary: When OAuth failed, a no-auth n8n MCP trigger was pasted into ChatGPT/Vapi; this weakens access control.
steps: On connector auth failure, stop | Report the block to Evens for re-auth
tools: n8n MCP Server Trigger, ChatGPT, Vapi
jarvis_use: Rule 6: never drop auth or route around a broken connector.

name: Discover, read schema, then execute with allow-once
summary: Search tools/workflows, get details (input fields, webhook), get human allow-once for side effects, execute, then check the result exists.
steps: search tools | get details / input schema | ask Evens before any side-effect verb | execute | read back the result
jarvis_use: Jarvis fills MCP inputs from the fetched schema and verifies the outcome before done.

name: Tool description is the routing contract
summary: Clients pick and fill tools from names/descriptions/schemas, so write each as if an unfamiliar model will call it; description plus manual enable acts as the ACL.
steps: Give each tool a descriptive name and purpose | Define required input fields | Review as a stranger model would
jarvis_use: Every Jarvis tool and procedural-memory skill gets a precise description with inputs.

name: Single-verb tools, read and write split
summary: Split capability into one-function tools named by verb (lookup, book, update, delete); separate read (check availability) from write (create event) with matching settings like time zone.
steps: Split capability into single-purpose tools | Name each by verb | Separate read and write tools | Match shared settings | Keep write behind HITL
jarvis_use: Jarvis MCP tools: one state change per tool; writes held for Evens.

name: Post-connect capability inventory
summary: After connecting, ask the agent to list available actions and what scope/account it sees; tag each as read/write and credit-costing; report gaps instead of assuming coverage.
steps: Prompt: check you can use X and list actions | Note credit-costing actions | Note read vs write | Report visible scope/accounts and gaps
jarvis_use: After any connector change Jarvis records a dated capability inventory tagged by cost and risk.

name: Coverage map: MCP vs UI gap handoff
summary: Record which product functions the MCP cannot do and do those steps in the UI, flagged.
steps: List needed actions | Check MCP coverage | Do uncovered steps in the UI and flag them
jarvis_use: Jarvis falls back to its Safari/computer tool for uncovered steps and logs it.

name: Multiple accounts per connector
summary: When a connector only sees one workspace, add another named connection signed in with a different account.
steps: Ask what the connector can see | Add another named connection | Owner signs in with the other account
jarvis_use: Jarvis reports scope gaps; Evens adds accounts.

name: n8n MCP bridge (instance-level, Claude / Claude Code)
summary: Enable n8n Settings > MCP access (OAuth or token), connect Claude's native n8n connector or Claude Code; tools: search_workflows, get_workflow_details, execute_workflow.
steps: Use a recent n8n version | Settings > MCP access on; choose OAuth | Copy server URL | Add the n8n connector in the client and approve OAuth | Mark only chosen workflows available
tools: n8n instance MCP, Claude connectors, Claude Code
jarvis_use: Jarvis calls n8n through MCP only after Evens re-auths the connector (reported failing with 401); no raw tokens.

name: One n8n MCP Server Trigger for many workflows, behind a voice front-end
summary: Group one-job workflows as tools of one MCP Server Trigger with per-tool descriptions and input schemas; a voice assistant picks which to call.
steps: Build each verb as a workflow | Attach them to one MCP Server Trigger | Describe each tool and define inputs | Add the MCP tool to the voice assistant
jarvis_use: If Jarvis needs a set of backend actions, group them behind one MCP server rather than separate HTTP tools.

name: Bearer header + SSE transport fallback
summary: Point the MCP client at the production URL, authenticate with a Bearer header, and switch to SSE if streamable HTTP fails.
steps: Use the production URL | Set Authorization: Bearer from an env var | Try SSE if streamable HTTP fails
jarvis_use: When wiring an MCP server, Bearer from env only, transport fallback to SSE.

name: Native mail connectors are read-only; send is a separate approved action
summary: Claude/ChatGPT Gmail connectors only search; a webhook-to-Gmail-send workflow exposed over MCP adds send.
steps: Draft in chat | Send only via a dedicated send tool | Evens approves each send
jarvis_use: Jarvis drafts; sends stay behind hard lock 2.

name: ChatGPT custom MCP connector via developer mode
summary: ChatGPT dev mode lets you create a custom connector with a server URL and OAuth; it warns about unverified connectors and failed live on tape.
steps: Enable developer mode | Create connector, paste URL, choose OAuth
jarvis_use: Failure-case reference only: report and stop when OAuth breaks.

name: Vendor event webhook into a local workflow
summary: Paste the production webhook URL into the vendor's developer settings and subscribe only to the completion event (Fireflies transcription complete).
steps: Copy the production (not test) webhook URL | Paste into vendor developer settings | Enable only the completion event
jarvis_use: Webhooks over polling; Jarvis has no inbound event trigger today.

name: Platform MCP for test runs instead of the browser
summary: Add the platform's MCP config so the coding agent can trigger and inspect runs itself; secrets go into .env.
steps: Add the platform MCP config | Ask the agent to trigger a test run | Supply secrets via .env placeholder | Check the runs page
jarvis_use: Prefer platform MCP over browser for triggering/inspecting runs.

name: Second agent verifies setup through the analytics MCP
summary: One person instruments the funnel; another checks the setup for errors via the PostHog MCP; experiments test whether changes move metrics.
steps: Instrument funnel events | A different agent reviews via the analytics MCP | Use experiments to test changes
jarvis_use: Builder does not check its own work; needs Jarvis's missing independent verifier.

name: MCP results are point-in-time facts
summary: MCP calls are stateless; store only verified facts and re-query for current state.
steps: Store each MCP result as a dated FACT | Re-query before acting on remembered state
jarvis_use: Procedural memory stores dated facts; Jarvis re-queries rather than trusting old results.

name: Scraping actor called on demand
summary: Keep scraping platforms as specialists; the agent invokes a specific Apify actor only when a task needs the data.
steps: Pick the specific actor | Invoke it inside the task | No standing loop
jarvis_use: Jarvis can call an Apify MCP actor for a scoped pull inside one job.

name: Zapier MCP bridge for apps missing from the plugin list
summary: Connect the Zapier MCP and expose specific app actions when no native connector exists (e.g. Beehiiv stats).
steps: Create a Zapier MCP server with needed actions | Owner authorizes | Call the actions and check output
jarvis_use: Option for Evens when no native connector; weigh against builder no-rent rule.

name: Channels: push phone messages into a running session
summary: An MCP server pushes Telegram/Discord/iMessage events into a running agent session for remote control.
steps: Install channels MCP | Connect messaging source
jarvis_use: Telegram is legacy in the hive; any channel needs Evens's OK.

name: Artifacts that call MCP connectors per viewer
summary: Private dashboards/apps that fetch and act through MCP connectors for each viewer; not on public shares.
steps: Build the artifact | Wire to connectors | Keep it private
jarvis_use: Possible connector demo surface; write actions stay HITL.

name: Research-to-publish automation through one MCP
summary: Run research, draft and publish inside chat through one vendor MCP.
steps: Connect the MCP | Research then draft | Publish only with approval
jarvis_use: Jarvis may chain research and draft; publishing is Evens's call.

name: Voice loop = STT -> LLM/tools -> TTS, stage-logged
summary: A voice agent is the ordinary text agent with speech-to-text in front and text-to-speech behind it, looping listen, transcribe, decide or call a tool, speak. Log each stage so failures trace to a stage.
steps: Capture speech | Transcribe (STT) | Send text to the operator loop with prompt and tools | Speak the reply (TTS) | Loop; log timestamps per stage
jarvis_use: Build Jarvis talk/Face as the same single operator loop with STT/TTS wrapped around it, not a separate voice brain; log per stage.

name: Barge-in (interrupt) acceptance test
summary: Talk over the agent mid-sentence; it must stop at once and take the new request. Latency and barge-in make it feel human.
steps: Start a conversation | Interrupt while it speaks | Check that it stops and handles the new request | Note latency
jarvis_use: Add as a Face voice acceptance check: an interrupt during TTS stops playback and routes the new utterance.

name: Spoken ack before slow tool calls (no dead air)
summary: Before a tool call, the agent says a short holding line; tool-call silence is measured and not shipped as 'human'. Some stacks go silent synchronously while a function runs.
steps: Prompt or config rule: say a holding phrase before any tool call | Measure silence while tools run | Use async or filler where supported
jarvis_use: Jarvis says a short status line via say before slow tools and logs the silent gap as a latency metric.

name: Visible thinking state during tool lookups
summary: While the agent looks something up, the face shows a thinking visual, so delay reads as work.
steps: Switch to the THINKING visual when tools run | Return to speaking when the answer is ready
jarvis_use: Face shows a think state during tool or memory calls; live :4018 changes need Evens's OK.

name: Full-screen face with listen/think/speak states and a minimal HUD
summary: One full-bleed animated surface whose center changes by state, plus a corner HUD showing connection, state and clock.
steps: Render a full-screen board | Swap the center element by state | Show state, clock and connection in a corner HUD
jarvis_use: Reference pattern for Jarvis Face (BUS300); prototype off-live, and only change :4018 with Evens's OK.

name: Wake word plus key push-to-talk trigger
summary: The mic listens for a 'JARVIS' wake word, or the user presses a key to talk; replies come back in voice.
steps: Keep the mic listening for the wake word | Offer a key as push-to-talk fallback | Speak the reply
jarvis_use: Match this trigger model for Jarvis voice input; the repo default (hold-Home push-to-talk) differs from what the tape shows.

name: Push-to-talk dictation with custom vocabulary
summary: Dictate long prompts instead of typing, often while looking at the thing being critiqued; add dictionary entries for names that get mistranscribed.
steps: Run a dictation tool or /voice | Speak the brief while looking at the output | Add custom vocabulary for mistranscribed names
jarvis_use: A local push-to-talk path into the same operator loop, with a vocabulary file for tool and person names. Vendor plugs (Glydo/Glido) are ads.

name: Normalize, read back and confirm before writes
summary: Normalize inputs (for example lowercase emails), read back name, email and phone spelling, and get a yes before calling a write tool. On one tape the read-back caught a misheard email. Skip NATO phonetics because they are too slow.
steps: Normalize inputs | Read back identifiers | Let the user correct them | Only then call the write tool
jarvis_use: Extend Jarvis's send/pay/delete hold to any identifier-bearing write: normalize, read back briefly, confirm through ask_owner.

name: Speech-to-speech model vs STT->TTS chain (free playground benchmark)
summary: Native speech-to-speech models (for example Gemini 3.1 Flash Live) process audio directly and claim lower latency and better tone handling. They can be tried for free in Google AI Studio before any integration.
steps: Open AI Studio > Live > Flash Live preview (free tier) | Run the same scripted prompts on both paths | Compare latency, interrupts, alphanumerics, tone | Write a decision packet
tools: Google AI Studio, Gemini 3.1 Flash Live
jarvis_use: For BUS300, benchmark S2S against Jarvis's chain on measured latency, barge-in, alphanumerics and tool silence; no private data on free tiers; no install without Evens's OK.

name: Done / needs-you notification cue
summary: A hook plays a sound or sends a notification when the agent finishes or needs the human.
steps: Hook on stop and needs-input events | Play a sound or post a notification
jarvis_use: Jarvis gives a short audible or notification cue when a job ends or blocks on ask_owner. Hooks are missing; say and done exist.

name: Four-part voice agent anatomy
summary: Spec every voice agent as a model/persona, a system prompt, a voice, knowledge, and tools (MCP, API, n8n, script).
steps: Pick the model | Write the prompt | Pick the voice | Attach knowledge | Attach tools
jarvis_use: Use as the BUS300 voice-slice spec checklist; knowledge retrieval is the weak part.

name: Voice agent grounded in your own content corpus
summary: Pull your transcripts into the agent's knowledge so it answers about your content. The 15-minute build time is unverified.
steps: Pull transcripts | Index them as knowledge | Expose a lookup tool | Test by voice
jarvis_use: Ground answers in Evens's corpus through a retrieval tool; this needs the missing signal-ingestion piece.

name: One engine, many front doors
summary: The same agent is reachable from a test console, a web widget or a phone number without rebuilding it.
steps: Build and test once | Expose via widget | Optionally connect telephony (gated)
jarvis_use: Keep one operator engine behind Face, Orb and any later phone surface.

name: Voice reply style: local timezone, concise, low temperature
summary: Tune voice replies to the owner's timezone, keep them short, and lower the temperature for consistency.
steps: Set the timezone rule | Ask for concision | Lower the temperature | Recheck tools
jarvis_use: Jarvis voice uses ET and short replies.

name: Live transcript and text fallback during voice
summary: Widget options: a real-time transcript and the ability to type during a call.
steps: Enable the live transcript | Enable text-while-on-call
jarvis_use: Options to consider for Jarvis Face.

name: Voice ramble prompt plus 'what am I not thinking about?'
summary: Dictate a loose description and end by asking the agent for questions and gaps you have not considered.
steps: Ramble the idea | Ask what is missing | Answer the questions
jarvis_use: Jarvis accepts voice dumps and replies with the gaps it sees before acting.

name: Per-task status indicator (working / idle / needs approval)
summary: An always-visible status shows each agent's current task, animates while working, and flags sessions needing attention or approval, with sounds on spawn and approval.
steps: Show each task's state | Animate while working, static when idle | Flag and sound on needs-approval
jarvis_use: Face/Orb shows a compact per-job state and plays a sound on approval requests (proposal; live Face changes need Evens's OK).

name: Calendar and task tools with a disambiguation question
summary: A voice agent reads the calendar, blocks time, and adds tasks, asking one question when the target (for example a workspace) is ambiguous.
steps: Define read and write functions | Read, then write | Ask when several targets match
tools: Google Calendar, ClickUp, Gemini Live API
jarvis_use: Ask one short disambiguation question before an ambiguous write; calendar writes under HITL.

name: Chunk TTS under 60 seconds to avoid voice drift
summary: Long single generations make a cloned voice drift, so generate segments under a minute and stitch them in order.
steps: Split under 60s | Generate each | Stitch in order
jarvis_use: Jarvis TTS for long replies is generated in short chunks and concatenated.

name: Vision grounding with stated confidence
summary: With webcam or screen share the voice model describes and answers about the scene; object IDs can be wrong.
steps: Enable screen or camera | Confirm what it sees | Treat IDs as fallible
jarvis_use: Screen-aware answers state what was seen and how confident Jarvis is, and confirm via page elements before acting.

name: Per-turn thinking level and grounding knobs
summary: Live session settings: voice, media resolution, thinking level, context size, function calling, search grounding.
steps: Thinking none for chit-chat | Higher for tool tasks | Enable search grounding for live facts
jarvis_use: Expose thinking level and grounding as per-turn routing knobs in Jev.

name: Phone dispatch to the desktop agent
summary: Pair the phone with the desktop, send a task remotely, and get notified when it is done.
steps: Pair the phone | Send a task | Notify on completion
jarvis_use: Jarvis takes a phone request, runs it on the Mac, and notifies Evens on completion.

name: Phone as remote for a running Mac session
summary: /remote-control bridges a local session to the phone app; work stays on the machine. Slash commands from the phone may fail.
steps: Run /remote-control | Open the session on the phone | Send prompts; avoid control commands
jarvis_use: A phone check-in channel for running Jarvis jobs, limited to plain prompts.

name: Event-trigger and two-way chat channels
summary: External events (webhooks, calendar bookings) trigger agent tasks one-way, or the agent is chatted with two-way.
steps: Connect a webhook | Map an event to a task | Optionally allow two-way chat
jarvis_use: Webhook events as Jarvis triggers (webhooks over polling); outbound replies follow the no-send rule.

name: Explicit first-turn policy (greet or wait)
summary: Configure whether the assistant speaks first with a fixed or generated greeting, or waits for the other person.
steps: Pick speaks-first or waits | Write the greeting
jarvis_use: Set Jarvis voice's first-turn behavior in config rather than leaving it to chance.

name: Sectioned agent prompt with if-X-do-Y branches
summary: Prompt sections: identity, style, injected context variables, task branches (wrong number, bad time), required topics, end rules, error handling.
steps: Identity | Style | Context variables | Branches | Required data | Stop condition
jarvis_use: Jarvis uses this layout when drafting agent prompts and grows the branches from failed runs.

name: Enable an explicit end action
summary: The end-call tool is off by default; turn it on so the agent has a clean terminal action.
steps: Open tools | Enable end call
jarvis_use: Jarvis has done; check default-off end/stop tools on any agent it configures.

name: Booking agent: blank assistant with exactly two calendar tools
summary: A job-named assistant gets only the tools the job needs: check availability and create event.
steps: Create a blank assistant | Set persona and goal | Add check-availability and create-event
jarvis_use: Scheduling needs read and write calendar tools; booking stays behind Evens's approval.

name: Check understanding and manage overwhelm
summary: Slow down when the listener loses the thread and keep asking whether it makes sense.
steps: Watch for lost-thread signals | Slow down | Ask if it makes sense
jarvis_use: Jarvis explains in chunks and checks understanding after each step.

name: Saved swappable persona instructions
summary: Named system-instruction profiles switch persona and tone at once.
steps: Create a named instruction | Write role and tone | Switch and test
jarvis_use: Named tone profiles (operator, briefing) over the same core loop.

name: Remote surface must show context and resets, or stay low-risk
summary: Messaging hides context usage, resets and slash commands; use it for low-risk tasks and keep deep work in the cockpit.
steps: Classify task risk | High risk goes to the main surface | Low risk is fine remotely
jarvis_use: Jarvis's voice/phone surface exposes context usage and session resets, or limits itself to low-risk tasks.

name: Voice note in, voice + text out
summary: The agent transcribes voice messages and replies with both text and a voice note.
steps: Receive voice | Transcribe | Reply with text + TTS
jarvis_use: The Jarvis voice channel returns both text and speech.

name: Embed a site voice widget snippet (knowledge widget)
summary: The widget is one HTML snippet the coding agent places on the site; a product-knowledge widget is tested on localhost with Q&A and interruptions.
steps: Copy the snippet | Add it to pages | Hard-refresh and test on localhost
jarvis_use: Jarvis places snippets through files/shell and verifies by reloading in Safari; localhost only, since a live embed is a deploy.

name: Use voice only where it replaces a person
summary: Voice daily briefs are costly theater; send routine status as short text and keep voice for where speech is the point.
steps: Ask whether voice replaces a human job | Otherwise send short text
jarvis_use: Routine status defaults to short text; voice is for interactive turns.

name: Talk-to-agent replaces click UX
summary: Thesis: ask an agent by voice or text and it answers from the data, instead of clicking through UI.
steps: Expose data to the agent | Query by voice or text
jarvis_use: Supports Jarvis's voice-first operator design.

name: Copyable deliverables as files or rendered panes
summary: Copy long text from the desktop app or extension, not wrapped terminal output; manage routines there.
steps: Write deliverables to files | Open them for the user
jarvis_use: Jarvis returns deliverables as files, not wrapped terminal text.

name: Inbound / outbound / website-widget voice types
summary: Sort deployments by who starts the call; widgets count as inbound, and outbound places calls.
steps: Decide who starts the call | Outbound needs approval
jarvis_use: Jarvis voice stays principal-started; outbound calling is a Tier-3 send.

name: Disclose AI identity and offer human handoff
summary: Third-party calls open with 'I am an AI assistant' and transfer to a human on request or when the caller is upset.
steps: Put the disclosure in the first line | Add a handoff path
jarvis_use: Jarvis does not speak to third parties today; if approved later, it self-identifies as AI and hands off to Evens.

name: Professional voice clone
summary: A clone trained on about 4 hours of the owner's voice is used as the agent voice.
steps: Record voice | Create the clone | Select it
jarvis_use: Reference only; voice clone or vendor spend needs Evens's OK.

name: Provision phone numbers for inbound/outbound assistants
summary: Create or import numbers (free US numbers per the speakers' claim) and link them to inbound or outbound assistants.
steps: Create or import a number | Assign inbound/outbound assistant
jarvis_use: Reference only; telephony is spend and send, gated behind Evens.

name: Telegram bot channel with user-ID allowlist
summary: Create a bot, get your numeric user ID, and allowlist only it.
steps: Create the bot | Get your user ID | Set the allowlist
jarvis_use: Telegram is a legacy channel (do not revive); the allowlist-only-Evens principle applies to any future remote channel.

name: Chat site assistant must capture the lead
summary: A site assistant should ask for contact details, not only answer Q&A.
steps: Answer | Ask for contact details | Record the lead
jarvis_use: Selling surface; locked while in BUILDING mode. The next-step capture idea applies to any future conversational build.

name: Custom themes via /theme
summary: Switch the Claude Code theme to auto, dark, color-blind friendly, or custom.
steps: /theme | Pick one
jarvis_use: Minor; only relevant if Jarvis drives Claude Code sessions for screenshots.

name: Jarvis as the default first surface
summary: Try every task, including non-code writing, recall and planning, in the one agent loop before opening a browser or app, so context and procedural memory build up in one place.
steps: Before opening an app, ask Jarvis | Route writing, recall and planning through the same loop | Let procedural memory build up from finished jobs
tools: Claude Code, Codex, VS Code, Cowork
jarvis_use: Jarvis is the default entry point; non-code asks go through the same operator loop.

name: Log every time he leaves Jarvis
summary: Each time Evens leaves the agent window to do something by hand, log it and turn the gap into a new connection or skill.
steps: Notice a manual exit | Log the task and the missing capability | Propose a connector or skill draft
jarvis_use: Jarvis logs the manual steps it sees or is told about and proposes the missing connector or skill.

name: Search across his sources
summary: Find a document someone sent without knowing which tool it is in, by searching all connected sources.
steps: Connect sources | Ask for the doc from a named person | Search every source read-only and merge the hits
jarvis_use: Search Gmail, Slack and Drive MCPs read-only. Parallel read-only tool calls are missing, so the search runs one source at a time.

name: Process mentor ("is this possible?")
summary: Describe a manual process and tool; the agent proposes automation options and tests them with you while you keep judgment.
steps: Describe process and tool | Ask how it could be done | Review and test the options together
jarvis_use: When Evens describes a process, Jarvis proposes options and runs a test with him rather than simply doing it.

name: Map recurring tasks to skills
summary: From a spoken list of daily and weekly tasks in your own domain, map each recurring task to a skill and turn suitable ones into routines.
steps: Evens describes his week by voice | Ask which tasks could become skills | Draft the skills | Propose routines only for approved ones
jarvis_use: Jarvis keeps an index of Evens's recurring tasks mapped to skills and proposes new ones. Blocked by the missing skills library loading.

name: Trigger audit
summary: List weekly tasks set off by something predictable (email type, weekday, new lead), rank them by frequency, skip high-risk ones, and automate the top one once it is battle-tested.
steps: List tools, repeated processes and their triggers for a week | Write each as 'when A, do X, Y, Z' | Rank by frequency and skip high-risk ones | Draft the top one for Evens's approval
jarvis_use: Jarvis builds the audit from shell history, calendar and mail, and proposes the top candidate as a draft only. No sends.

name: Wake on a message, plus a sparse heartbeat
summary: The agent wakes on each inbound message and on a periodic heartbeat to run checks, which gives an always-on feel.
steps: Choose an approved inbound channel | Wake on each message or webhook | Add a sparse heartbeat through the canonical scheduler | Reply on the same channel
tools: Open Claw, Hermes Agent, Telegram, Hostinger VPS
jarvis_use: Wake on events over an approved channel. Telegram and OpenClaw are legacy and must not be revived, and the heartbeat must use the existing scheduler (no new scheduler).

name: Phone as a remote control
summary: Drive the same local desktop agent session from a phone, with messages synced both ways, including computer-use instructions.
steps: Expose the session through an authenticated link | Open it on the phone | Phone messages feed the same session
tools: Claude Code remote control, Claude dispatch, Codex remote
jarvis_use: The phone is a thin client into the same Mac operator session, with the same approval gates. No remote OS-level changes without confirmation on that turn.

name: Pending actions with a stop window
summary: The human sees what agents are about to do, not just how many are busy, and can stop it in time. One compact place to approve or deny, with live usage and cost.
steps: Queue every held action with effect, target, reversibility and cost | Show the queue in one place | Approve or deny in one step
jarvis_use: Holds, ask-then-resume and a cost meter exist. Missing: one place listing pending consequential actions with their effect and cost. No menu-bar app.

name: Permission scopes: once / session / always
summary: Permission prompts offer once, session or always, and 'always' is granted only for the routine action an unattended job needs.
steps: Prompt with scope options | Record the grant with its action class | Expire session grants
jarvis_use: Jarvis holds actions for OK but has no scope on grants. 'Always' should be limited to narrow, reversible classes; Tier-3 actions are never 'always'.

name: Human approval on sends and outreach
summary: Humans stay in the approval and feedback loop as trust grows. Voice and outreach actions need an explicit confirmation (one source adds a PIN).
steps: Draft the action | Require an explicit yes | Then execute
jarvis_use: Jarvis holds send, pay and delete buttons for Evens's OK. The PIN variant is not present.

name: Human picks the problem, the agent executes
summary: Value moves to judgment and problem selection; use AI as a team of agents, not a search box.
steps: Evens picks the problem | Jarvis executes | Evens judges the result
jarvis_use: Jarvis asks Evens for direction and acceptance (ask_owner/done) and does the execution.

name: Shoot and return (background delegation)
summary: Trigger a scoped job, work elsewhere (another monitor or task), and come back to a finished result.
steps: Persist job state to disk after each step | On restart, offer to resume unfinished jobs | Run native-app steps through Accessibility in the background | Notify with a receipt when done
jarvis_use: Shell background jobs and the Safari background tab work. The computer tool is foreground only (it takes his screen), there is no Accessibility control for native apps in the background, and no resume after reboot, so the job is lost when the Mac restarts.

name: Proactive risk scan
summary: Agents scan the CRM, inbox and project tools for cold deals or late projects, flag them and propose fixes, acting only where permitted.
steps: Scan connected tools read-only | Detect risks | Propose fixes for Evens's OK
jarvis_use: Surface flagged risks with proposed fixes only. No autonomous sends or changes. Building mode means no sales motion.

name: Ops monitoring and self-repair
summary: The agent watches background systems and fixes breakages overnight instead of paging a human.
steps: Give read visibility into services | Diagnose on failure | Report and propose a repair
jarvis_use: Possible later. Repairs touching live surfaces (:4018, the Orb, deploys) stay behind Evens's approval.

name: Diagnose its own broken connector
summary: Tell the agent a channel is broken; it investigates with its own terminal, finds the root cause and reports or restarts.
steps: Evens states the symptom | Jarvis investigates with the shell | Report root cause; restart only with OK | Retest
jarvis_use: Jarvis can diagnose with the shell and report the root cause. Restarts of live surfaces need OK, and connectors must not be routed around (rule 6). Not proven live.

name: Idea council
summary: Several persona agents (skeptical buyer, competitor-pricing researcher, math stress-tester) review an idea and merge a verdict, its weak points and the cheapest test.
steps: Define the personas | Run each on the idea with research tools | Merge into a verdict, weak points and the cheapest test
jarvis_use: Advice only. Without sub-agents, Jarvis could run the personas one after another in its single loop.

name: Persona file with a pushback trait
summary: An editable persona or soul file, kept apart from facts and procedures, loaded each turn, with a 'push back on bad ideas' trait. It is changed only through explicit feedback.
steps: Keep tone in its own file | Include a pushback trait | Edit only on explicit feedback, with OK
jarvis_use: JARVIS_CONTEXT exists, but editing it changes the live prompt (rule 17a), so changes need Evens's OK and a backup.

name: "Show me X" puts a file on screen
summary: A spoken request for a specific asset: the agent finds it on disk, displays it and confirms by voice.
steps: Receive the spoken request | Search local files | Open the result | Confirm by voice
jarvis_use: Shell/files search, then open, then say. Tools exist; a live match against the demo has not been captured.

name: Say when to use each tool
summary: Attaching tools is not enough. The prompt or procedure names which tool to call at each step and what to send, and an LLM-drafted prompt is checked for this section before use.
steps: Draft the prompt or procedure | Check for a per-step tool policy | Add branches (if X then tool A)
jarvis_use: Procedural memory entries and any prompt Jarvis writes should name the exact tool for each step.

name: Procedures written as scripts with preconditions
summary: Write procedures like call-center scripts with conditional branches, plus a short numbered rule block (resolve the contact first, always reply with a status, don't ask what you can look up).
steps: Write the action order and branches for each scenario | Add numbered precondition rules | Always return a status line, even on a no-op
jarvis_use: Store procedural memory as explicit scripts with branches and precondition rules, not loose goals.

name: No formatting leaks in output
summary: Remove markdown and bold tokens from prompts so they don't leak into generated text, then check the rendered output.
steps: Remove formatting tokens from prompts | Check the rendered output
tools: n8n AI Agent, ChatGPT, Wispr Flow
jarvis_use: Strip formatting before say and before any drafted outgoing text.

name: Meet him where he already works
summary: The assistant lives in the surface the user already uses (e.g. Slack), with retrieval, task actions and routine admin behind it.
steps: Pick his existing surface | Connect retrieval and task tools
jarvis_use: Jarvis meets Evens on his Mac, through voice and the Face, and could reach him on approved channels later.

name: Member concierge with per-person history
summary: One concierge agent handling onboarding, events, guest passes and support for many members, with running per-member history and MCP-exposed tools.
steps: Define member tasks | Keep a history for each member | Expose capabilities through MCP
jarvis_use: A multi-member client product. Jarvis serves Evens only, and BUILDING mode means no selling.

name: Morning brief
summary: A daily brief pulls the calendar, tasks, priorities and actionable Gmail, then drafts a plan with time-block suggestions, refined from feedback. It doubles as a starter template.
steps: Read today's calendar and actionable mail | Draft the plan with block moves | Store his feedback in memory | Schedule later through the canonical scheduler
jarvis_use: On demand today via the Gmail and Calendar MCPs, read-only, as a draft that is never sent. Scheduling must go through the existing scheduler with OK.

name: Own the foundation
summary: Build the second brain on the base harness with your own memory, hooks and skills, rather than adopting a third-party agent system.
steps: Start from the base harness | Add your own memory, hooks and skills layers
jarvis_use: Jarvis's loop and memory are owned and inspectable; it borrows ideas from OpenClaw and Hermes without adopting them.

name: Model decides how long research runs
summary: Give search_web and read_url tools plus a done criterion; the model decides how many searches and reads to run.
steps: Give search and read tools | Ask for a full brief | Let the model choose the loop count
jarvis_use: web_search and fetch in the operator loop, with a done criterion instead of a hardcoded pipeline.

name: Current date and time in context
summary: The minimal system context is the current date and time, so relative scheduling ('today 2 p.m.') works.
steps: Add the ET date and time to the turn context | Test a relative-time request
jarvis_use: Confirm that Jarvis injects the current ET date and time into each turn. It is not listed in the current harness description.

name: Ask Jarvis about itself; a link goes to read-then-propose
summary: Ask the agent about its own features (it reads its own docs), or paste a post link and say 'read this and help me implement it'.
steps: Answer self-questions from its own docs | Fetch the linked content | Write a packet | Propose; Evens approves
jarvis_use: Answer from its repo docs and skills index rather than guessing. Link-to-proposal needs the missing signal ingestion (YouTube/X transcript, frames, packets).

name: Clean strings in tool payloads
summary: When model text fills a tool query or body, clean or escape it (or tell the model to send plain text) so the JSON doesn't break; ground answers and cite sources.
steps: Escape strings before building payloads | Ground answers with tools and cite sources
jarvis_use: Escape model strings put into JSON and into Safari eval JS payloads.

name: Think before asking or acting
summary: A think step before asking follow-up questions and between tool or sub-agent calls: plan, resolve, think again, act.
steps: Plan | Check memory and files before asking | Act, then re-plan with the result
jarvis_use: Before ask_owner, check memory and files; write a short plan step between multi-step tool calls.

name: Specialist bots in group chats
