summary: Named specialist agents (inbox triage, chief of staff, invoice, content) in group chats handing work to each other.
steps: One brief per role | Written handoff notes inside one loop
jarvis_use: Jarvis is one general operator. It can play named roles with written handoff notes but does not spawn parallel bots.

name: Handoff routing and standing handoff rules
summary: A handoff tool routes to internal specialists or humans by destination description, without blocking on missing identity; new roles write their standing 'send me X' rule.
steps: Describe each destination by when to hand off | Write standing routing rules into memory
jarvis_use: ask_owner covers the human handoff. Missing: routing to sub-procedures by description, and writing down which inputs route to a new skill.

name: Brief + reference example → skill
summary: Create a new routine from a description of its duties plus a reference artifact (e.g. a PDF) so its outputs always match that style.
steps: Take Evens's description | Attach the reference artifact | Save as a skill | Check the first output against the example
jarvis_use: When Evens defines a routine, save the brief plus the example as a skill. Needs skills library loading.

name: Resolve contact → draft → hold
summary: Research a topic, resolve the recipient from a contact source of truth, pass the content to an email step, then verify the recipient and structure.
steps: Research | Resolve the contact | Draft | Hold for OK | Verify the draft's recipient and structure
tools: n8n AI agent, Perplexity, Claude Sonnet 4.5
jarvis_use: Jarvis resolves contacts from a source of truth rather than guessing, drafts, and stops for Evens's OK before sending. It runs these steps serially, without sub-agents.

name: Find the procedure from intent
summary: The user states a goal without naming a workflow; the agent searches its workflows and tools, reads the matching procedure and runs it.
steps: Search the procedure store for the goal | Read the best match | Execute it
jarvis_use: Match the request against procedural memory and skills by search, not by phrase routes. Needs skills library loading.

name: Calendar window rules
summary: Query explicit windows (now to 23:59:59 for today, a full day for future dates), treat the results as busy time, report only free slots, never event titles.
steps: Build an explicit time window | Read busy blocks | Report free slots only
jarvis_use: When checking calendars, query explicit windows and report free slots without other events' details.

name: Scheduled runs in isolated sessions
summary: Sitting work stays in the main harness. Scheduled runs are fresh isolated sessions with no recursive spawn and a timezone self-check; when one misbehaves, check memory freshness first.
steps: Fresh session per run | No recursive spawn | Timezone check | Check memory freshness first
jarvis_use: If Jarvis gets scheduled runs, each runs in a clean session through the existing scheduler; debug stale memory first.

name: Agent-driven install from docs URLs or vendor commands
summary: Give the agent a tool's URLs or the vendor's install/auth/skills commands. It reads the docs, installs prerequisites (e.g. Go) and runs the commands, and the browser OAuth goes to the human.
steps: Collect the tool's doc and repo URLs or the vendor's install/auth/skills commands | Run the install gate (license, archived status, last push, pin) | Have the agent install prerequisites and run the commands | Hand the OAuth step to Evens | Confirm the account and skills are visible
jarvis_use: Shell + web_fetch + Safari login handoff already cover the mechanics; the gate and post-install check are not coded steps.

name: Pre-install code vetting checklist
summary: Before installing an extension or repo, check: verified publisher, a real author, stars and forks. Review the code for outbound calls, exfiltration, shell injection, suspicious deps, secret handling, file-system access and remote script loading.
steps: Confirm the marketplace publisher is verified | Confirm the author's identity | Check repo stars and forks | Review the code for network calls, exfiltration, shell injection, dependencies, credentials, file-system access, remote scripts | Install only if nothing turns up; YELLOW goes to Evens
jarvis_use: Add these items to Jarvis's rule-18 install gate as a coded step.

name: Verify wiring after install
summary: An install can succeed with no runtime wiring (claude-mem SDK via npm leaves hooks unregistered). After importing linked parts, click or ping each one. Report installed only when hooks, MCP and links are live.
steps: Use the documented install path, not a partial library install | List the registered hooks, MCP servers or launch agents | Open or ping each linked tool or workflow | Run one real call before reporting installed
tools: claude-mem, n8n, Google Drive, Google Sheets
jarvis_use: Jarvis can run status commands via shell, but there is no independent verifier before done.

name: Install a skill from a GitHub URL
summary: Paste a skill repo URL into the agent and say 'add this skill', then invoke it.
steps: Find the skill repo | Run the install gate | Paste the URL and add the skill | Invoke it
jarvis_use: Blocked on skills-library loading, which Jarvis lacks.

name: Credential hygiene: named keys, .env from .env.example, env-only secrets
summary: Name keys and credentials by purpose. Copy .env.example to .env and have the owner fill it. Keep keys in .env, never in shared CLI scripts or repos. Delete demo keys afterward. Check presence only.
steps: cp .env.example .env | Owner creates keys and fills the placeholders | Name each key and credential by purpose | Check presence and length only, never print values | Check no secrets are committed before sharing a repo | Flag temporary keys for rotation
jarvis_use: Jarvis flags secrets today; a presence-check helper and a pre-commit secret check are not confirmed.

name: Prompt-injection scan before importing third-party agent or skill files
summary: Before installing community subagent markdown (e.g. awesome-claude-code-subagents), scan it for injected instructions with a read-only verifier that has no network access.
steps: Browse the curated repo | Run a read-only, no-network scan of each file | Install only clean files
jarvis_use: Needs sub-agents or a read-only worker, which Jarvis lacks; gate for anything entering procedural memory.

name: Global vs project scope for skills and agents
summary: Project agents and skills live in <repo>/.claude and are shared with anyone who clones it. Global ones in ~/.claude work everywhere. Meta-skills (skill-creator, frontend-design) are installed at user scope so they fire on their own. Move the file to change scope.
steps: Put team-shared skills in the repo, personal ones in the home dir | Install meta-skills at user scope | Move the markdown file to change scope
jarvis_use: Small global meta set always loaded, domain skills per job; depends on skills-library loading.

name: Provider API key creation (owner-only)
summary: Console steps for creating keys: a Google Cloud project with YouTube Data API v3 enabled and a restricted key, or the Anthropic console with billing and a named key. The key value goes into .env or an n8n credential.
steps: Open the provider console | Enable the API or add billing | Create a named key and restrict it to the one API | Owner pastes the value into .env or the credential
tools: Google Cloud Console, YouTube Data API v3, Anthropic Console, n8n
jarvis_use: Safari can walk the steps with login walls handed to Evens; snapshots could expose the key value, so redaction is needed.

name: Clone a starter agent-OS repo and run its guided setup
summary: Clone a template or full-stack agent repo into a folder and run 'set me up'. A one-time interview or audit builds the folders and installs the optional parts (vault, voice, face). It adopts the existing vault and identity instead of creating a second home.
steps: Run the install gate on the repo | Clone it | Run the setup interview | Detect and adopt the existing vault and paths | Configure only the chosen optional pieces
jarvis_use: Jarvis can clone and run via shell; the adopt-existing-brain rule should shape any Jarvis installer. Sibling repos stay uncloned.

name: New workspace scaffold
summary: Create an empty folder and trust it. Have the agent create CLAUDE.md and .claude/ (settings, agents, skills), or drop in a template CLAUDE.md and say 'read it and set up the project'. Review the agent's summary.
steps: Create the folder | Seed a router file and .claude/ or drop in a template | Have the agent build the structure and the .env | Review the summary it returns
jarvis_use: The files tool can do it; there is no named 'new workspace' procedure yet.

name: Check version and feature toggles before calling something missing
summary: If a model or node is not visible: update the CLI or app (then /model), or enable verified community nodes and restart (n8n Tavily). Only then fall back.
steps: Check the installed version | Update if behind | Check feature or community toggles | Restart and recheck | Only then fall back to raw HTTP or another tool
jarvis_use: Shell can check; make it a procedure. Model or config changes need Evens's OK.

name: Google Workspace CLI install with manual OAuth
summary: The agent installs gws from its repo. The human creates a GCP project, an internal consent screen and a Desktop OAuth client. The JSON goes into ~/.config/gws, then gws auth login, then enable the Drive, Gmail, Calendar, Docs, Sheets and Slides APIs, then a test search.
steps: Install gate, then the agent installs gws | Owner creates the GCP project, consent screen and Desktop client | Place the JSON in ~/.config/gws | gws auth login (owner approves scopes) | Enable the needed APIs | Test with a search
jarvis_use: One CLI for mail, calendar and docs; Evens does the OAuth click via the Safari handoff. Whether it is installed on the Mac is UNKNOWN.

name: Re-check vendor free tier at build time
summary: A plan named Yelp Fusion as free, but the tier was gone at build time and the agent switched to SerpAPI. Re-verify vendor availability and terms, then flag the cost to the human.
steps: Plan names a source | At build time check it is still available and free | Swap and update the .env placeholders if not | Owner confirms any paid switch
jarvis_use: web_search + ask_owner exist; make the re-check a step before using any vendor.

name: GitHub + Vercel deploy pipeline via CLIs
summary: Ask the agent to find and add the GitHub and Vercel CLIs, create the repo and connect hosting for a live URL. Later changes deploy by asking.
steps: Describe the goal and the tools | Agent adds the CLIs; owner logs in | Create the repo and connect hosting | Hold every deploy for Evens's OK | Verify the live URL
jarvis_use: Shell can run it; whether shell deploy commands get the same approval hold as Safari's send/pay/delete is UNKNOWN. Deploys are Tier-3.

name: Setup script before the agent launches
summary: A fixed script runs at session start, before the agent, to install packages, so the agent run doesn't spend time on setup.
steps: Write the setup script | Attach it to the job or environment | It runs before the agent loop starts
jarvis_use: A per-job pre-step; relates to the missing hooks and resume-after-reboot.

name: Own-stack remap; BLOCKED card instead of a vendor install
summary: Reproduce the demo's result on owned tools: map each vendor on the tape to an owned skill, bot or browser tool. If a needed tool is missing, file BLOCKED (tape tool, house remap, workaround, blocking yes/no) and stop. Install only what the owner names.
steps: List the vendors on the tape | Map each one to an owned shell, MCP or Safari equivalent | If none, write a BLOCKED card | Stop; install only on the owner's say-so
jarvis_use: Jarvis can remap by hand; the BLOCKED card format is not coded and its signal ingestion is missing.

name: Plugin marketplace install from the terminal CLI
summary: Marketplaces install only from the Claude Code CLI: claude, /plugin, marketplace, add URL, install, reload. The plugin then works in the desktop app and VS Code too.
steps: Install gate on the marketplace | Run claude in the terminal | /plugin, add the marketplace URL | Install the plugin and reload
jarvis_use: Interactive TUI; Jarvis would drive it via the computer tool or a non-interactive CLI flag, after the gate.

name: CLI factory: site or API to Go CLI plus skill
summary: A CLI factory researches a site, catalogs its features, generates a Go CLI, checks it by dogfooding, runtime checks and scoring, then wraps it in a skill. Demo: Hacker News.
steps: Install Go | Prompt the factory with the site link | Review the feature catalog | Generate and build the CLI | Dogfood and score it | Test through the skill
jarvis_use: Wrap Evens's own APIs only (no ToS-violating reverse engineering); needs skills loading and the install gate.

name: Custom domain DNS A-record hookup
summary: Add the domain in the host, choose automatic config, add the given A records in the registrar's DNS, wait for propagation, then deploy to the domain.
steps: Add the custom domain in the host | Copy the A records | Add them in the registrar's DNS | Wait | Deploy (Evens's OK)
jarvis_use: Safari can walk GoDaddy; DNS and deploy changes stay Evens-approved.

name: Path hygiene for file and log watchers
summary: A watcher silently missed the log while the folder was 'Herk 2.0'. It worked as 'herk-2'. Avoid spaces and periods in project folder names.
steps: Rename to lowercase with hyphens | Avoid spaces and periods | Retest pickup
jarvis_use: A debugging heuristic for procedural memory when a watcher misses events.

name: Install/run the coding-agent front end; the files are the product
summary: Use Claude Code through the VS Code extension, desktop app or CLI on a paid plan. Open a project folder. The front end is interchangeable because the project files stay the same.
steps: Check what is already installed | Install the extension, desktop app or CLI if missing | Owner signs in with a paid plan | Open the working folder
tools: VS Code, Claude Code extension, Claude Code desktop
jarvis_use: Jarvis keeps state in plain folders and can check installs via shell; sign-in is Evens's.

name: Port a project between harnesses
summary: Projects are files on GitHub. Open the project in another agent, ask it to understand and update it, and swap CLAUDE.md for AGENTS.md.
steps: Push to GitHub | Open in the new agent | Prompt it to analyze and adapt | Swap or mirror the instruction files
jarvis_use: The fleet already uses single-source rules with thin per-harness pointers.

name: Swap the model backend via settings env
summary: In .claude/settings.local.json env, point the Anthropic base URL at a compatible provider, use the provider key as the auth token, and set the default models (GLM 5.2 shown). Harness is the car, model is the engine.
steps: Get a provider key (owner) | Set the base URL, auth token and models in env via env var references | Relaunch and confirm the banner model
jarvis_use: Jev already routes across provider pools; a new vendor needs Evens's OK.

name: Enable an experimental flag via project settings.local.json
summary: Agent teams are off by default. Paste the env JSON from the official docs into the project's .claude/settings.local.json.
steps: Read the official docs JSON | Get Evens's OK | Write it to the project's local settings | Confirm the entry
jarvis_use: Files tool can do it; treat it as a config change needing Evens's OK, scoped to the project.

name: 21st.dev copy-prompt components
summary: Browse 21st.dev, click Copy prompt on a component, and paste it to the agent with integration instructions so it rebuilds the element.
steps: Open 21st.dev | Find the component | Copy its prompt | Feed it into the build
jarvis_use: Safari tool can open, click and read the prompt.

name: Bypass-permissions toggle
summary: Turn on 'allow dangerously skip permissions' in the Claude Code settings and use bypass mode after the plan is approved.
steps: Do not copy; use scoped allowlists
jarvis_use: Against Evens's rules; Jarvis uses scoped allowlists and approval holds.

name: VPS hosting: root install vs one container per agent; one-click n8n
summary: Install an agent at the VPS root or as one Docker container per agent (own memory, tools, keys), or self-host n8n through a managed one-click VPS. Know whether you are in the host shell or the container shell.
steps: Reference only | Any hosting spend needs Evens's approval | If sub-agents are ever hosted, one container each
jarvis_use: Jarvis runs on the Mac; keep the container-per-agent idea for future sub-agents.

name: Beamhook media-key app picker
summary: An open-source macOS tool to choose which app the media keys control.
steps: Check license and last push | Install only with Evens's OK | Pick the target app
jarvis_use: A Mac utility candidate, not a Jarvis capability.

name: Watch a social/YouTube video in his browser and save a watch packet
evidence: Safari tool has tabs/click/eval/read; signal ingestion (transcript, frames, contact sheets, write packets) is listed as missing.
summary: Reuse the existing tab (no new tab), play, verify currentTime advancing and unmuted, enable the auto caption track, sample frames at an interval, mark caption gaps explicitly, leave the ad player paused, write watch.json.
steps: List tabs and reuse the target tab | Snapshot and click Play | Sample paused/currentTime/muted several times; fail if not advancing | Enable the caption track and read cues via eval | Screenshot frames at a fixed interval | Write watch.json + contact sheet into a repo packet
jarvis_use: Jarvis watches a video in Evens's Safari by page elements, reads the caption track, samples frames and writes a packet; gaps are marked, not filled.

name: Verify-after-act card (ACT/EXPECTED/OBSERVED/COMPARE/NEXT)
evidence: Jarvis takes a fresh screenshot/snapshot after acts but has no structured expected-vs-observed record.
summary: After every click/type/navigate, observe state and compare against the stated expectation; a miss leads to a capped retry or escalation; OBSERVED is never invented.
steps: Write ACT and EXPECTED before acting | Act | Capture OBSERVED (snapshot text, location.href) | COMPARE match|miss | NEXT proceed|retry|escalate
jarvis_use: After each Safari or computer act Jarvis records expected vs observed from the fresh snapshot before the next step.

name: Use the output like a user, with proof screenshots and a hard iteration cap
evidence: Safari and computer tools plus shell exist; missing an independent verifier before done and an explicit per-task cap.
summary: For web outputs, start the site, drive it like a user (Playwright/agent-browser/in-browser), screenshot each result as proof, iterate on what is wrong, and obey explicit bounds (one run ignored a 5-game cap).
steps: Run the command that starts the site | Drive it like a user | Screenshot each result | Check the bound was obeyed | Iterate on defects | Hand the evidence to a verifier
jarvis_use: Jarvis opens web work in Safari, interacts, saves proof screenshots, enforces a step cap, and checks the render before claiming done.

name: Click-live flow file with a per-step card and RUN.md on disk
evidence: No flow runner; skills library loading is listed as missing.
summary: A browser verification flow is a file: app URL, hard_step, host, status, then ordered steps (launchApp/navigate, scroll, tapOn, swipe, assertVisible), each with a target, expected state and verify card. No expected state means no act. A chat 'looks good' is not a run.
steps: Create flows/{id}.yaml | Each step: id, verb, target, expected, verify_card | Never add a step that submits the hard-step form | Execute on the host browser, write a card per step | Write RUN.md with STATUS
jarvis_use: Jarvis loads a flow file, drives Safari through it, and writes cards plus a RUN status to disk.

name: Local fixture page to prove a click landed
evidence: No driver self-test exists in the harness.
summary: Self-test browser actuation on a static page bound to 127.0.0.1 with a reveal button that shows a hidden token; curl 200 is not a click, only the token appearing after the click passes.
steps: Write fixture HTML with #reveal and hidden #observed token | python3 -m http.server 8765 --bind 127.0.0.1 (background job) | curl expects 200 (not a click) | Click #reveal via the Safari tool | Snapshot: #observed visible with the token
jarvis_use: Jarvis self-tests its Safari driver (and real-mouse clicks) on a local reveal page before claiming browser control works.

name: Retry cap 2, no silent driver switch, escalate with the exact blocker
evidence: Repetition brake and escalation exist; no per-target retry cap or no-substitution rule.
summary: When the browser host fails, retry at most twice, never substitute another browser stack silently, never invent a click, log each act/result, mark HOLD and escalate with a concrete ask.
steps: Log each host act/tool/result | Stop at retry 2 | Do not substitute another browser stack | Escalate with the concrete blocker
jarvis_use: If a Safari act fails twice Jarvis stops, reports the exact error via ask_owner, and does not switch drivers.

name: Fetch-first probe, then headed browser
evidence: shell/web_fetch exist; the ladder and UNKNOWN labeling are not codified.
summary: Before opening a browser on a site, curl apex/www/http, robots/sitemap/healthz, sweep common routes and string-assert the first-paint HTML (H1, CTAs, forms, money hrefs). If no headed pass is possible, mark visual steps UNKNOWN and the status failed (host missing).
steps: curl apex, www, http and record codes/redirects | Probe robots.txt, sitemap.xml, healthz | Sweep key routes | Extract title/H1/CTAs/forms/money hrefs | Mark headed UNKNOWN until a real browser pass
jarvis_use: Jarvis audits any site with shell curl first and uses Safari only for what needs a real click; it never claims visual results without a Safari pass.

name: Capped click path that walks to the hard step and asserts it without pressing
evidence: Safari already holds send/pay/delete for OK; no click budget or verifier.
summary: Walk the real CTA path with a click budget and a card per click, all the way to the submit/pay control. Assert it is visible, never press it, record that the hard step was not executed, and hand the grade to a separate verifier.
steps: Set hard_step (send/pay/publish) | Lock the existing tab | Click CTAs with a card each, within a budget | assertVisible on the submit control, do not press | Record budget used and hard step not executed | Separate verifier grades
jarvis_use: Jarvis tests contact/sign-up/checkout paths in Safari up to the final button and hands the press to Evens.

name: QA stress test of a build
evidence: Tools exist; no QA routine or bug-list output format.
summary: Open the app where the human can watch, click every control, try to break it, and return a bug list (dead links, bare empty states, visual-only states), then plan and fix.
steps: Open in a visible browser | Click everything, stress-test | Collect findings | Plan fixes, execute
jarvis_use: Jarvis drives its background Safari by page elements to QA builds and returns a bug list.

name: Fallback ladder when a page fetch is blocked
evidence: web_fetch and the Safari read exist; the fallback order is not codified.
summary: When a direct scrape is blocked (YouTube), switch to a structured alternative such as RSS plus per-page extraction, and report which method worked.
steps: Try a direct fetch | On a block, try RSS/API | Then a Safari DOM read | Report the path used
jarvis_use: On a blocked fetch Jarvis tries RSS, API, or a Safari DOM read before giving up, and says which path worked.

name: Press Enter when a click only focuses
evidence: Safari key action exists; the fallback is not automatic.
summary: If a click on a link/button only focuses it and the URL is unchanged, press Enter and re-observe the URL/H1; record it as 'match (retry Enter)'.
steps: Click target | If URL unchanged and focused, key Enter | Re-observe URL and H1
jarvis_use: Jarvis falls back to Enter on a focused element when a Safari click does not navigate.

name: Press Escape when a modal won't close
evidence: Safari key action exists; the fallback is not automatic.
summary: If the Close click only focuses the X and the dialog stays, press Escape and verify the workspace is visible.
steps: Click Close | If the modal persists, key Escape | Verify the workspace is visible
jarvis_use: Jarvis tries Escape when a dialog close button does not dismiss it.

name: API first, browser driving only as fallback
evidence: mcp, shell and Safari tools exist; connector rule 6 covers the guardrail.
summary: Use the vendor API/MCP; when a needed setting is not exposed (HeyGen avatar engine) or there is no API, drive the web UI, verify the setting took, and switch back to the API once it is exposed.
steps: Use the API when the option exists | Detect the gap | Drive the web UI as a stopgap | Verify the setting | Return to the API when available
jarvis_use: Jarvis prefers API/MCP and drives Safari elements only for authorized accounts when no API exposes the setting; never to route around a broken connector.

name: Signed-in sessions stay with the human
evidence: The Safari tool hands login walls to him with ask-then-resume.
summary: Log in once (human handles captcha/2FA); sessions persist for many sites but banks expire; check signed-in state in a fresh session; the human can take over the same browser.
steps: Human signs in once | Check signed-in state at job start | At a login wall, hand it to Evens and resume
jarvis_use: Jarvis drives Evens's already-signed-in Safari, checks signed-in state first, and hands login walls to him; it never enters credentials.

name: Detect a looping fix and change strategy
evidence: The repetition brake stops identical repeats; no strategy switch on repeated failed fixes.
summary: When an assistant guiding a GUI build (n8n node by node) keeps repeating failed fixes, stop and switch approach (docs, course).
steps: Track fix attempts per symptom | On a repeat, stop | Switch to docs or another approach
jarvis_use: When guiding Evens through a GUI build, Jarvis detects repeated failed fixes and switches strategy.

name: Bilingual step targets
evidence: Safari find exists; there is no alternate-label matching.
summary: Cards name both FR and EN labels (Connexion/Sign In, Brouillon/Draft) so flows survive a UI language change; note the observed language.
steps: List the target in both languages | Match whichever is present | Record the UI language
jarvis_use: Jarvis finds elements by alternate FR/EN labels when the page locale varies.

name: Alias/redirect canonical check and retiring duplicate flows
evidence: Doable with curl/Safari; there is no flow catalog.
summary: When a route becomes a 308 alias, shrink its flow to launching the alias and asserting the canonical URL; retire duplicate walk steps with a pointer.
steps: Launch the alias | Assert the canonical URL | Mark the other steps RETIRED with a pointer
jarvis_use: Jarvis keeps one test flow per real page and checks redirects instead of duplicating walks.

name: Element-targeted comments on a live page
summary: Preview the built page in an embedded browser, select elements, leave visual comments that become edit prompts.
steps: Open the page | Select an element | Comment | Send as an edit prompt
tools: Codex in-app browser, Claude in Chrome, Claude Code desktop browser pane
jarvis_use: Jarvis takes element-targeted feedback from Evens on a Safari page and turns it into edits.

name: Headed vs headless runs
evidence: Safari runs in a background tab; the computer tool is foreground.
summary: Visible runs to watch and build trust; background runs for long jobs without disturbing the user.
steps: Use visible for new flows | Use background for routine runs
jarvis_use: Background Safari tab for routine runs; the foreground computer tool when Evens wants to watch or the flow is new.

name: Reuse the existing tab, no new tab
summary: Lock onto the already-open tab or navigate in place; record the tab id.
steps: Find the tab at the URL | Navigate in place | Record the tab id
jarvis_use: Jarvis drives Evens's existing Safari tab rather than spawning windows.

name: Read location.href on SPA navigation
summary: The snapshot URL lagged Next.js client navigation; read location.href via JS as the observed URL.
steps: After the click, eval location.href | Use it as OBSERVED
jarvis_use: Jarvis reads document location via Safari eval to confirm SPA navigation.

name: Drive the browser from the session that owns the tabs
evidence: Single operator loop; sub-agents are missing, so this holds by construction.
summary: Sub-agents could not see the parent's browser tabs; the click passed only from the owning chat (list, lock, snapshot, click, snapshot, unlock).
steps: List tabs from the owning loop | Snapshot, act, snapshot | Do not delegate browser acts to sub-agents
jarvis_use: Jarvis drives Safari from its main loop; when sub-agents are added, browser acts stay with the owning loop.

name: Cookie-bound jobs stay local
evidence: Jarvis runs on the Mac against his Safari.
summary: A Playwright job relying on local cookies failed on a stateless cloud routine; keep it local or pass auth in the request from env.
steps: Classify whether the job needs a cookie jar | If yes, keep it local | If remote, pass auth via env
jarvis_use: Jarvis's Safari jobs depend on Evens's logged-in session, so they stay on the Mac.

name: Agent password manager fills logins
evidence: Hard lock: no secrets in files; login walls are already handed to Evens.
summary: Import a CSV of credentials into the agent's built-in password manager so logins are filled without the password in chat; 2FA stays manual.
steps: Do not import credentials into Jarvis | Hand login walls to Evens
jarvis_use: Jarvis never holds passwords; at most a credential-request flow where Evens approves in his own password manager.

name: Actuation ladder: API/MCP, then fixed script, then page elements, then screen vision
summary: Before any UI job, write the tier choice and reason. Use an API/CLI/MCP if one exists, a fixed macro if the click path never changes, and vision browser or screen use only when the UI needs reasoning. Merged with 'agent over SaaS UI' and 'computer use only for apps without connectors'. One source notes an exception: it used the browser for X despite an API, for formatting, media and per-use cost reasons.
steps: Write LADDER (api|mcp|script|safari|screen) and WHY before acting | Try API/CLI/MCP | If the path is fixed, script a deterministic macro | If the UI varies, use Safari page elements, then screen vision | Stop at 2FA/admin/money
tools: Codex desktop, Codex plugins, Claude Code, Clay
jarvis_use: Jarvis tries MCP/API first, then shell/AppleScript or a fixed script, then Safari page elements, and screen computer use last, writing the ladder choice before the first UI action.

name: 2FA, admin and secrets stay human
summary: Stop at 2FA codes, admin elevation, OS security prompts and password-CSV imports, then hand control to the human. Watch money paths with the browser visible. A saved session is not permission. Do not auto-read texted codes with computer use.
steps: Detect a 2FA/admin/secret prompt on screen | Stop acting | ask_owner with what is on screen | Resume only after Evens acts
jarvis_use: Jarvis treats any 2FA, CAPTCHA, password or OS security prompt as a hard stop in both the Safari and computer tools and hands control to Evens. Safari already does this for login walls; the computer tool does not yet.

name: Native desktop-app control with safety stops and a scope check
summary: Ask the agent to open a desktop app and change an in-app setting. It says its stop conditions (admin password, security permission), shows a visible border while driving, refuses OS privacy permissions, and changes only the in-app setting.
steps: State target app, intended change and stop conditions | Drive with the visible overlay cursor | Refuse OS security/privacy settings | Fresh screenshot and AX read after the run to confirm scope | Report what changed
jarvis_use: Jarvis uses the screen computer tool for native apps without an API. It says its stop conditions first, refuses OS security settings, and checks after the run that only the intended scope changed. Background control through Accessibility is still missing.

name: Computer-use product QA with structured bug reports
summary: The agent opens the built app, clicks around, and logs bugs with severity, expected vs actual, repro steps and a triage summary.
steps: Prompt: QA the app I just built | Agent explores the live surface | Log bugs with severity, expected vs actual, repro, screenshot | Triage summary
jarvis_use: Use this bug-report schema for Jarvis screen-QA runs, produced by an independent verifier pass before done.

name: Screen critique (roast) as a separate grader pass
summary: Share the screen with an assistant and ask it to critique the live page (likes and dislikes). It reads the page visually and gives the critique.
steps: Open the built page | Screenshot it | Separate grader critiques it | Act on the critique
jarvis_use: After building, Jarvis screenshots the live page and runs a critique (layout, CTA, clarity) as a separate grader step, not in the builder's own context.

name: Agent-driven app testing on simulator or live device
summary: Run an iOS app in a simulator panel next to the conversation, or let the agent exercise features on a live device from one prompt with no scripts or selectors.
steps: Build and run the app; simulator opens | Prompt the agent to exercise the features | Observe and record the results on the real surface
jarvis_use: Jarvis tests on the real surface (a simulator window or the screen) through the computer tool, not only in unit tests. A simulator-aware tool and a verifier step are missing.

name: Granted-folder file agent
summary: Point a sandboxed agent, with read/write only to granted folders, at a messy folder with one instruction: sort by type, rename consistently, and write a summary.
steps: Grant access to named folders only | Give a one-shot outcome instruction | Refuse writes outside scope | Report a change summary
jarvis_use: Jarvis runs file chores only inside folders Evens names and ends with a change summary.

name: Docker-sandboxed agent for risky OS/file work
summary: Run an agent (Agent Zero) in a Docker sandbox for OS, file and privacy-sensitive tasks.
steps: Start a throwaway container with the named folder mounted | Run the risky command inside | Copy back only the reviewed results
jarvis_use: Jarvis runs risky or unknown shell experiments in a throwaway container with only the named folder mounted, not on the Mac host.

name: Slow-down / wait-for-idle harness for real-time UIs
summary: To let an agent verify fast software such as a game, expose commands to start it and slow or step frames, so the agent observes, thinks, then takes one action at a time and verifies the way a user would.
steps: Expose start and slow/step controls | Wait for idle before each action | Observe, think, take one action | Verify as a user would
jarvis_use: Before each screen action, Jarvis waits for the UI to go idle (or steps animations). Safari has wait; the computer tool does not.

name: Supervise from a second monitor and nudge
summary: Run the agent on one monitor while working on the other, and nudge it when it drifts, because it is nondeterministic.
steps: Keep the agent visible on a side monitor | Glance at its to-dos and actions | Nudge when it veers
jarvis_use: Jarvis posts short progress receipts at each step change so Evens can steer without watching every action. say/ask_owner and idle continuation already exist; a regular receipt format does not.

name: Use screenshots instead of typing descriptions
summary: Models read images, so send a screenshot instead of describing what is on screen.
steps: Take a screenshot | Attach it to the reasoning step
jarvis_use: Jarvis screenshots the screen region in question instead of asking Evens to describe it.

name: Find a local file by description, confirmed visually
summary: Describe a half-remembered file. The agent searches local folders with several keyword variants, opens candidates to confirm the right one, returns the path, and offers to copy it into the project.
steps: Describe the file and likely folder | Search with keyword variants | Open the candidate and confirm visually or by content | Return the full path; offer to copy or organize
jarvis_use: For 'find that file' requests, Jarvis searches with Spotlight/mdfind or find, confirms by content or by opening and screenshotting, and returns the path.

name: Bare Hands gesture interface over local folders
summary: Webcam hand tracking with no gloves (pinch zoom, spin, flick, claw-then-fist pull) over panels mapped to real folders on disk.
steps: Map panels to local folders | Open files as on-screen elements | Gesture to scale, rotate or close
jarvis_use: Parked. The folder-backed panel idea could inform a file-browsing Face mode later.
